title: Asking About a Room Change
transcript:
Student: Hi, I wanted to ask about switching rooms. My roommate and I have totally different schedules.
Advisor: I see. Have you two tried a roommate agreement? Setting quiet hours sometimes helps.
Student: We did, back in September. It lasted about a week.
Advisor: Okay. Room changes open on November first, but spaces are limited.
Student: Is there a waiting list I can get on now?
Advisor: There is. Fill out this form and list three buildings you'd accept. The more flexible you are, the better your chances.
Student: Got it. I'll put down every building, then.

questions.stem: What does the student imply about the roommate agreement?
options: It was never signed by his roommate.
It was suggested by his parents.
It did not solve the problem for long.
It is required before a room change.
questions.explanation: He says the agreement "lasted about a week," meaning it didn't really work.

questions.stem: According to the advisor, how can the student improve his chances of moving?
options: By being willing to live in several buildings
By finding a new roommate himself
By explaining his schedule in writing
questions.explanation: The advisor says, "The more flexible you are, the better your chances."
